note: Curated questions. Each answer is a fact taken from a story on the site and carries the same source. More questions are generated from the country and bloc data at build time.

questions.q: On the usual Mercator world map, Greenland looks as big as Africa. How many times larger is Africa in real area?
questions.explain: On the map Greenland looks as big as Africa, while Africa's real area is 14 times larger. The projection inflates land the farther it lies from the equator.

questions.q: Greenland's real area is comparable to that of which single African country?
options: The Democratic Republic of the Congo
questions.answer: The Democratic Republic of the Congo
questions.explain: Greenland's real area is comparable to that of the Democratic Republic of the Congo alone.

questions.q: In 2025 the African Union supported a campaign to replace Mercator's map with which projection?
questions.explain: The campaign was led by Togo, whose foreign minister called it a scientific discussion, not a political one. Equal Earth keeps areas in proportion.

questions.q: Africa looks roughly the size of South America on the Mercator map. How much larger is it really?
options: More than one and a half times as large
questions.answer: More than one and a half times as large
questions.explain: Africa looks roughly the size of South America, but is more than one and a half times as large.

questions.q: Which script did the Kingdom of Aksum develop?
questions.explain: Aksum developed its own script, Ge'ez, later changed to mark vowels so that it became an abugida.

questions.q: Most of the manuscripts kept in Timbuktu are written in which language?
questions.explain: Most are in Arabic. Some are in African languages such as Fula, Songhay, Tamasheq, Bambara and Soninke, written in the Arabic script, a practice known as Ajami.

questions.q: Some Timbuktu manuscripts are in African languages. Which script do they use?
questions.explain: Writing African languages in the Arabic script is known as Ajami.

questions.q: In the third century Mani counted Aksum among the four great powers of the world, alongside Persia, Rome and which other?
questions.explain: Mani, the founder of Manichaeism, counted Aksum alongside Persia, Rome and China.

questions.q: Which king made Christianity the state religion of Aksum in the mid-fourth century?
questions.explain: Under King Ezana the kingdom adopted Christianity as its state religion, around 325 by one count.

questions.q: Why do historians doubt the claim that Mansa Musa was the richest person who ever lived?
options: His wealth cannot be calculated accurately: the figures come from one chain of Arabic reports
Historians found his treasury and counted it
He gave all his gold away before he died
questions.answer: His wealth cannot be calculated accurately: the figures come from one chain of Arabic reports
questions.explain: Historians such as Hadrien Collet argue his wealth cannot be calculated. Estimates of the gold he carried all come from the same chain of Arabic reports, and turning them into modern money is regarded as unsound.

questions.q: About how much of the gold circulating in the medieval Mediterranean is estimated to have come from West Africa?
questions.explain: It is estimated that two thirds of the gold circulating in the medieval Mediterranean came from West Africa.

questions.q: Did every historian agree that Mansa Musa's gift-giving in Cairo caused a crisis in the price of gold?
options: No: Warren Schultz argued the fall was within the normal swings of the price
Yes, and it lasted a century
No source mentions the price of gold at all
questions.answer: No: Warren Schultz argued the fall was within the normal swings of the price
questions.explain: The chronicler al-Umari reported a fall in the price of gold, but Warren Schultz has argued it was well within normal swings in Mamluk Egypt.

questions.q: Injera is traditionally made from the flour of which cereal?
questions.explain: Teff is a cereal that originated in Ethiopia and is mostly eaten in Ethiopia and Eritrea.

questions.q: How long is injera dough fermented with its starter, ersho?
questions.explain: The dough is fermented with a starter called ersho, kept from earlier batches, for 24 to 72 hours.

questions.q: What is the large round griddle that injera is cooked on called?
questions.explain: The batter is poured in a spiral onto a large round griddle called a mitad. The mesob is the basket where injera is kept; ersho is the starter.

questions.q: What is the original Senegalese dish that jollof rice is traced back to?
questions.explain: The original dish, thieboudienne, has rice, fish, shellfish and vegetables. The fishing communities of Saint-Louis are considered its birthplace.

questions.q: Which two countries' rivalry grew into the friendly "Jollof Wars" in the mid-2010s?
questions.explain: The rivalry was strongest between Nigeria and Ghana, with cooking competitions and social media campaigns.

questions.q: How many countries in Africa does the World Bank give figures for?
questions.explain: The World Bank gives figures for 54 countries. The African Union counts 55 members, because it includes the Sahrawi Republic.

questions.q: Roughly how many times more people does Nigeria have than Seychelles?
questions.explain: Nigeria has about 237.5 million people and Seychelles about 122,700. The ratio is calculated from the World Bank's 2025 estimates.

questions.q: About how many languages does Glottolog list with Africa as their only macroarea?
questions.explain: Glottolog lists 2,373, or 2,264 after leaving out placeholder entries and sign languages. Some are no longer spoken.

questions.q: Which language family holds the most African languages in Glottolog?
questions.explain: Atlantic-Congo holds 1,407 of the 2,264, about 62%. Afro-Asiatic comes second with 313.

questions.q: Did the Berlin Conference of 1884–85 itself divide Africa between European powers?
options: Yes, it drew the borders on a single map
No: it set rules for claims, and the partition came later
No, it was only about trade in Europe
questions.answer: No: it set rules for claims, and the partition came later
questions.explain: The article says the conference "did not actually divide the continent" but gave a framework by which Africa could later be partitioned.

questions.q: How many African kingdoms or states sent representatives to the Berlin Conference?
questions.explain: Fourteen states were represented, and there were no representatives from the African kingdoms, states and cultures whose territories were affected.

questions.q: About what share of people in Africa lived in urban areas in 2023?
questions.explain: About 672 million of about 1,478 million people, calculated from World Bank figures. In 23 of the 54 countries more than half were urban.

questions.q: Which of these countries had the highest urban share of its population in 2023?
questions.explain: Gabon was at about 92%. Malawi, at about 17%, had the lowest of the 54.

questions.q: Which of these countries had the highest GDP per person in 2023?
questions.explain: About $18,131, in current US dollars. The lowest was Burundi at about $250.

questions.q: In which year did Ethiopia defeat Italy at the Battle of Adwa?
questions.explain: The battle was fought on 1 March 1896. Italy then signed the Treaty of Addis Ababa, which recognised Ethiopia's sovereignty.

questions.q: Which two African countries were outside European control in 1914?
questions.explain: By 1914 the whole continent, apart from Abyssinia (Ethiopia) and Liberia, came under European control.

questions.q: According to the University of Chicago, who controlled all of Egypt in what became the Twenty-Fifth Dynasty, after Kashta took over Upper Egypt?
questions.explain: Kashta took over Upper Egypt, followed by his son Piankhi, who controlled all of Egypt in what became known as the Twenty-Fifth Dynasty.

questions.q: What did the fourteenth-century traveller Ibn Battuta call Kilwa?
options: One of the most beautiful towns in the world
A city of gold and ivory only
questions.answer: One of the most beautiful towns in the world
questions.explain: National Geographic History quotes Ibn Battuta calling Kilwa one of the most beautiful towns in the world.

questions.q: Where did cassava originate?
questions.explain: Wild populations are centred in west-central Brazil. Portuguese traders introduced it to Africa in the 16th century.

questions.q: Who founded the Poto-Poto School of Painting in Brazzaville in 1951?
questions.explain: A French amateur painter. Nicolas Ondongo and Guy Léon Fylla led the cooperative formed after 1960, and Félix Ossali is the painter whose blue birds, in Lods's account, started it.

questions.q: What opened at Constitution Hill in Johannesburg on 21 March 2004, Human Rights Day?
questions.explain: The old prison there had closed on 31 January 1983. Constitution Hill opened to the public the next day.

questions.q: How many volumes can the Bibliotheca Alexandrina hold, before using compact storage to expand?
questions.explain: Up to 4 million volumes, and 8 million with compact storage, say the architects.

questions.q: In Zakouma National Park, about how much did the elephant population fall between 2002 and 2010?
questions.explain: From more than 4,000 elephants in 2002 to about 400 in 2010, a drop of 90 per cent. It has since recovered.

questions.q: In December 2021 UNESCO added which Senegalese dish to its list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
questions.explain: In Wolof, ceebu jën means "rice with fish". UNESCO said the recipe and techniques are traditionally passed down from mother to daughter.

questions.q: In Botswana, seswaa, a pounded meat dish for weddings and funerals, is described as prepared mainly by whom?
questions.explain: A student writing about Botswana says it is prepared by men; another source describes several people pounding the meat together.

questions.q: What is the base of cachupa, the stew linked with Cabo Verde?
questions.explain: Corn like hominy is boiled for hours and combined with beans, meat or fish, and vegetables.

questions.q: In a genome study of 77 Afrikaners, how many had no evidence of non-European ancestry?
questions.explain: Only a single individual out of 77 had no evidence of non-European admixture; the average non-European share was about 5 percent.

questions.q: In a 2015 study of US ancestry, about what share of European Americans had 1 percent or more African ancestry?
questions.explain: About 3.5 percent of the 148,789 European Americans in the study carried 1 percent or more African ancestry, up to 12 percent in Louisiana and South Carolina.

questions.q: When the European Economic Community was founded in 1957, what did it include besides its six member states?
options: Their colonial possessions, such as the Belgian Congo
questions.answer: Their colonial possessions, such as the Belgian Congo
questions.explain: Hansen and Jonsson show that the EEC comprised the six states and their colonial possessions, which it called overseas countries and territories.

questions.q: What did Italy's 1940 law on meticci bar Italian fathers from doing?
questions.explain: A report to the Italian parliament says the 1940 law expressly barred the Italian father from recognising his mixed-race child.

questions.q: In Pew's 2008-09 survey, which of these countries had the largest share of adults saying they believe in witchcraft?
questions.explain: 93% in Tanzania said yes, against 37% in Nigeria, 27% in Kenya and 17% in Ethiopia. Belief varies a great deal from country to country.

questions.q: What does the UN human-rights office say states should criminalise?
options: Accusations of witchcraft and ritual attacks
questions.answer: Accusations of witchcraft and ritual attacks
questions.explain: The High Commissioner's report says witchcraft itself should not be criminalised, but ritual attacks and harmful acts related to accusations should be.

questions.q: Where is Coffea arabica indigenous?
options: Highland cloud forests of Kaffa, Ethiopia
questions.answer: Highland cloud forests of Kaffa, Ethiopia
questions.explain: Coffea arabica is indigenous to the highland cloud forests of Kaffa in south-western Ethiopia.

questions.q: In 2020, which group of countries jointly inscribed couscous on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage List?
questions.explain: Four countries submitted couscous together in 2020: Algeria, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia.

questions.q: According to the sources in this story, what did colonial indirect rule do to African social groups?
options: Gave them their names for the first time in history
questions.explain: Colonial indirect rule codified and hardened fluid identities into bureaucratic 'tribes' to simplify taxation, policing and labour.

questions.q: What did maize, brought from the Americas, largely replace in the making of ugali-type porridges?
questions.explain: Ugali (also sadza, nshima, pap) became dominant after American maize replaced ancient indigenous millets and sorghums.

questions.q: What do wild honeyguide birds do for human honey hunters?
options: Lead them to hidden wild beehives
questions.answer: Lead them to hidden wild beehives
questions.explain: Wild honeyguides recruit and lead human foragers to wild beehives, and recognise the signals that the hunters use.

questions.q: How long was one term of the Oromo Abbaa Gadaa?
questions.explain: The Gadaa system ran on eight-year cycles, and the Abbaa Gadaa and his cabinet had to step down at the end of their single term.

questions.q: What does the Asante Golden Stool represent, and who may sit on it?
options: The king's throne; only the king
The collective soul of the Asante nation; nobody
A trophy of war; the governor
questions.answer: The collective soul of the Asante nation; nobody
questions.explain: By Asante religious law nobody may sit on the Golden Stool. In 1900 a British demand to sit on it sparked war.

questions.q: Which Nigerian town is recorded as having one of the highest rates of fraternal twin births in the world?
questions.explain: Igbo-Ora in Nigeria records up to 50 twin sets per 1,000 live births, according to the BBC and Reuters reports cited in the story.

questions.q: Why is the Dogon Togu Na built with a very low ceiling, about 1.2 to 1.5 metres?
options: So disputants must stay seated and talk instead of brawling
questions.answer: So disputants must stay seated and talk instead of brawling
questions.explain: The low ceiling prevents angry people from standing up, so everyone has to remain seated and look for a verbal compromise.

questions.q: In traditional Tuareg culture, who wears the tagelmust veil?
questions.explain: Men wear the tagelmust from adulthood, while women do not cover their faces.

questions.q: What licence did the Chewa Nyau masked dancers enjoy?
options: To mock and discipline corrupt chiefs and colonial rulers in public
questions.answer: To mock and discipline corrupt chiefs and colonial rulers in public
questions.explain: The dancers enjoy spiritual immunity to publicly criticise leaders, including colonial rulers.

questions.q: What does the self-name Amazigh (plural Imazighen) mean, according to the reference entry cited?
questions.explain: The entry glosses Amazigh as 'free people'. 'Berber' is the outsiders' word.

questions.q: Which of these are names for the same community?
questions.explain: 'Fulbe' is used in their own languages and 'Peul' in French; Fula and Fulani are the English names.

questions.q: Besides Nigeria, in which two West African countries do major Yoruba populations live?
questions.explain: The source describes major Yoruba populations in Nigeria, Benin and Togo.

questions.q: How did the number of people counted as Maasai in Kenya's census change between 1969 and 2019?
questions.explain: Kenya counted 154,906 Maasai in 1969 and 1,189,522 in 2019. Part of the change is the growth of the whole population; the share rose from 1.43% to about 2.5%.

questions.q: Which generic term for these peoples was adopted by San organisations in 2003?
questions.explain: San organisations (WIMSA, 2003) adopted 'San'; in Botswana the official term is Basarwa. The author notes the context and the wishes of the people named matter.

questions.q: Which script is Afaan Oromo written in?
questions.explain: Afaan Oromo uses the Latin alphabet, while Amharic and Tigrigna use the Ge'ez script.

questions.q: In Geschiere's accounts of the Maka of Cameroon, where is the djambe said to live?
questions.explain: Geschiere describes the djambe as a substance or small aggressive animal that lives in a person's belly. The same idea appears for the Beti, Duala and Bakweri under other names.

questions.q: According to Geschiere, to which kind of witchcraft do the 'invisible plantations' stories belong?
options: A newer form tied to trade and new wealth
questions.answer: A newer form tied to trade and new wealth
questions.explain: In that form, victims are turned into zombies and made to work on invisible plantations. Geschiere links it to European trade and the new rich, and says it reached the Maka region only recently.

questions.q: According to UN DESA and IOM data, where do the majority of African international migrants live?
questions.explain: Roughly 20.8 million African migrants live in another African country, compared to about 19.5 million residing outside Africa worldwide.

questions.q: What did the UN Commission of Inquiry find to be the primary cause driving Eritreans to flee their country?
options: A desire for higher urban wages
questions.explain: The UN Commission of Inquiry on Human Rights in Eritrea documented that national service can last for decades under military discipline and forced labour, leading European authorities to grant Eritreans asylum recognition rates above 80%.

questions.q: How many deaths and disappearances has the IOM Missing Migrants Project recorded in the Mediterranean Sea since 2014?
questions.explain: Over 30,000 lives have been lost or reported missing in the Mediterranean since 2014, with over 23,000 deaths on the Central Mediterranean route alone.

questions.q: What did empirical labor economic studies (such as Card on the Mariel Boatlift or Foged & Peri) find regarding native employment?
options: Little to no negative effect on native employment and wages
A permanent 50% collapse in native wages
Widespread mass layoffs of native professionals
Complete elimination of minimum wage protections
questions.answer: Little to no negative effect on native employment and wages
questions.explain: Empirical studies show that immigration induces task specialization and occupational upgrading among natives without causing aggregate job losses.

questions.q: How do annual remittances sent home by the African diaspora compare to foreign aid (ODA) and direct investment (FDI)?
options: Remittances consistently exceed both foreign aid and foreign direct investment
Remittances are negligible compared to foreign aid
Remittances equal less than 1% of foreign direct investment
questions.answer: Remittances consistently exceed both foreign aid and foreign direct investment
questions.explain: According to the World Bank and KNOMAD, remittance flows to Sub-Saharan Africa exceed  billion annually, surpassing Official Development Assistance and Foreign Direct Investment combined.
